open_obligations: Compare the assumptions of Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 (Appendix A) with Anil et al.'s Theorem 2 to confirm they are strictly weaker
Check that both theorems assume a comparable prover hypothesis class (all deterministic mappings)

Note that Anil et al.'s Theorem 2 is stated for verifier-leading sequential PVG formulations in which the problem instance is revealed after the verifier picks its strategy, and its sufficiency argument has the verifier switch to the complete and sound verification system, while Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 is stated for their PVG with a role-conditioned (helpful/sneaky) prover, utilities RV and RP and equilibrium (v*, h*, s*); check that these settings match before relying on the extension
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al.'s Theorem 2 links verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria to complete and sound protocols; the authors state that their Theorem 1, for their PVG with H the set of all deterministic mappings, has more relaxed assumptions on the loss function and reward than Anil et al.'s Theorem 2.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Equivalence of verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria with complete and sound protocols, under weaker loss and reward assumptions

text: The authors prove that, for an unrestricted deterministic prover class, a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of their PVG is necessary and sufficient for completeness and soundness. They state that compared to Theorem 2 in Anil et al. their result has more relaxed assumptions on the loss function and reward.
title: Kirchner et al.'s Theorem 1 has more relaxed assumptions than Anil et al.'s Theorem 2
